# swift-fakable

> A Swift macro (`@Fakable`) that generates a `fake()` factory method on structs and enums for building test fixtures. MIT licensed, supports Swift 6.0+.

swift-fakable provides a single `@Fakable` macro that you attach to a struct or an enum. It generates a `static func fake(...)` wrapped in `#if DEBUG`:

- On a **struct**, one parameter per stored property, in declaration order, each defaulted by its type, forwarded to the memberwise initializer.
- On an **enum**, a parameterless `fake()` returning the first case without associated values, or the first case with its values defaulted when every case has them.
- Tests name only the values they care about: `Item.fake(itemId: "item-1", price: 500)`.

## Default Values

- `String` → `""`
- `Int`, `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int32`, `Int64`, `UInt`, `UInt8`, `UInt16`, `UInt32`, `UInt64` → `0`
- `Double`, `Float`, `CGFloat` → `0.0`
- `Bool` → `false`
- `T?` / `T!` → `nil` (checked before the type name)
- a generic parameter of the enclosing type → no default; the parameter is required
- `[K: V]` → `[:]` (checked before array)
- `[T]` → `[]`
- anything else → `.fake()`, so nested models compose when each is `@Fakable`

Matching is on the written spelling, so a type alias for `String` resolves to `.fake()`, not `""`.

## Key Features

- Structs and enums, with or without associated values
- Access-level-aware generation, `private` through `public`, including `package`
- Optional and implicitly unwrapped optional properties
- Arrays and dictionaries, including nested generic spellings
- Labeled and unlabeled enum associated values
- Nested `@Fakable` models through the `.fake()` fallback
- Generic structs (generic-typed properties become required parameters) and generic enums

## Limitations

- `fake()` mirrors the memberwise initializer: `static` properties, computed properties, and constants that already have a value are skipped, while `willSet` / `didSet` observers stay included
- Struct properties need an explicit type annotation; inferred properties are skipped
- `fake()` calls the memberwise initializer, so a custom `init` in the same file breaks it (declare it in an extension)
- Only structs and enums; anything else is a compile-time error
- A generic enum is an error only when every case carries a generic associated value, since `fake()` takes no parameters; a case with no associated values or with non-generic ones is used instead
- The `#if DEBUG` guard is not configurable

## Requirements

- Swift 6.0+
- macOS 10.15+ / iOS 13+ / tvOS 13+ / watchOS 6+ / visionOS 1+
- MIT License
